title: Promoting inclusive pathways to employment for people with disabilities, businesses, and inclusion service providers guided by the principle of 'place—train—employ inclusively'.
summary:
The pilot project run by Projekt Router helps people with disabilities find suitable jobs in the general labor market and establish themselves there in the long term. The focus is on getting people into work as early as possible and then providing them with individualized support directly in the workplace, helping them gain the necessary skills, and, when needed, acting as a mediator between them, their coworkers, and the company. It is also important that the coaching be provided as consistently as possible by the same coach, so that trust can develop and reliable support can be offered throughout the various phases.
The research component examines how participants, employers, and job coaches experience this approach. To this end, quantitative questionnaires, individual interviews with participants, and focus groups with employers and job coaches are used. The study focuses, among other things, on expectations, support needs, stress, satisfaction, quality of life, professional development, and collaboration within the workplace.
The findings are intended to show what facilitates or hinders workplace inclusion and how existing support services can be improved.
